body:
PR #2039 F1 FIXED AND PUSHED — d419a4aa68. Your falsification run both ways:

    stub write_hold out of the recording path
      OLD test  still PASSES   (it wrote the hold itself)
      NEW test  FAILS          "a refusing verdict must leave a merge-hold on the PR"
      restored  passes

The test now records through `handle_review_record` and asserts the three
consequences the RECORDING PATH owns: PR held, verdict blocking, spec parked at
NeedsAttention with a failure_reason instead of left Done.

NOW THE PART YOU NEED, AND IT IS A LIVE-REPO INCIDENT I CAUSED AND CLEANED UP.

The first version of the fix set AIDA_DRIVE_ROOT to a tempdir, which is the
obvious way to drive that function. It is not sufficient. The hold is written to
`protection_root`, which PREFERS AIDA_PROJECT_ROOT and only falls back to the
resolved root — and a seat shell has AIDA_PROJECT_ROOT set to the real
repository. So the test wrote into the live repo:

    .aida/merge-holds/PR-1452        created
    .aida/review-verdicts/PR-1452.json   created
    real PR #1452 (MERGED)           labelled aida:merge-hold via gh

All three removed; #1452's labels are now empty. Confirmed clean.

THE GENERAL HAZARD, which is bigger than this test: `handle_review_record`
reaches AMBIENT environment for its write root, so any test driving it from a
seat shell writes to the real store and calls the forge — silently, and with a
PR number of the test author's choosing. The remedy is to pin BOTH roots at the
tempdir, which also disarms the forge call for free (sync_label resolves the
forge from that root, finds none in a bare temp dir, returns Ok without shelling
out). That is now documented in the test body rather than left to be
rediscovered.

I think this is also the charitable explanation for WHY the original test called
the two primitives directly. Not laziness — the path it should have driven has
side effects that escape a tempdir unless you know about the second env var. It
does not excuse a vacuous test, but it is worth knowing before the same shape
appears in another aftermath test.

I am NOT filing a spec for it per the operator's instruction. If you want one it
is yours to open; the evidence above is complete enough to file from.

NEXT: PR-1998's watch.rs rebase conflict unless you redirect me. Say if BUG-1532
should jump ahead of it now that #2034 and #1984 have landed.
subject: PR #2039 F1 fixed, falsification runs both ways (d419a4aa68) — plus a live-repo incident I caused and cleaned: the test wrote to the REAL store and labelled merged PR #1452
